what: Two layers laid over a base-color button (say orange and blue) tilt 16° on hover and slide together to the lower left (−16, 100px), revealing the base (navy). Like the original design-tool layout animation, the layers’ position (left·top) is moved first, then the transform for the moved amount is released to 0 over .4s cubic-bezier(.44,0,.56,1) (measured: 40px button 80 · 48px 100 · 78px button −32/140 · 32px arrow cell −8/70). On release it plays in reverse, and for a finger, while pressed

options.[data-fx-part=layer]: Covering layers (children, fill the button) — the first is behind, the second in front. Color is set in the user’s css
options.[data-fx-part=label]: Text (child) — sits on top of the layer
options.--fx-dx · --fx-dy: Distance at which layers peel away (via style), default -16px · 100px
options.--fx-dx2 · --fx-dy2: Distance the front layer alone moves off (via style), default same as the back layer
options.--fx-rot2: Front layer tilt (via style), default same as the back layer
options.dur · ease: Duration and curve (options), default .4 · 0.44,0,0.56,1 — duration can also be passed via --fx-dur (seconds, through style) (Brand .36s: matched to the measured 300~350ms of the original .4s tween)
options.host: Ancestor selector that receives the interaction — moves when the whole link is hovered, like the arrow cell inside a ‹Details› link (brand .py-more)

use: Button

from.where: shared.css .py-btn (header·Hero·Contact section button — navy background, orange·blue layers)

note: If gsap is present, fx.js moves the position and clears the transform like the original, if not, fx.css reaches the same end shape with :hover translate · rotate transitions
